cards.explanation: The answer is his own disciples. The text says John "…sent his disciples" to ask Jesus his question (Matthew 11:2-3). From inside a prison he can't go himself, so his own people carry it for him. No phone, no group chat, just good friends with good legs.

John wants to know if Jesus is the One who was to come. The disciples ask Him, "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" (Matthew 11:3). It's a direct question, and I love that it gets asked out loud. Jesus doesn't brush it off, and we'll see what He sends back.

The answer is True! Jesus lists it right in the report: "…the dead are raised…" (Matthew 11:5). That's in the middle of the list, not at the end. It sits right between the deaf hearing and the good news going to the poor, like it's one more item. It's quite a list, friends.
The answer is poor! Jesus finishes the report with "…the good news is preached to the poor." (Matthew 11:5). It's the last item on the list. I wish I'd had that kind of news in the back of my drawer.

The blessing is for whoever doesn't fall away because of Him. Jesus says, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me." (Matthew 11:6). That's how He wraps up His answer to John, who asked his question from prison. I think that's a tender thing to say to a man sitting in a cell. The blessing is for the one who does not fall away.

The answer is kings' palaces. Jesus says, "Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces." (Matthew 11:8). Palaces are the place He names for fine clothing. He's asking the crowds what they went out to see, and I love how He walks them through it.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't stop at prophet. He says, "Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet." (Matthew 11:9). He said yes to the question, then added something bigger. That's why "nothing more" is false.

The answer is prepare! Jesus quotes the words: "Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You." (Matthew 11:10). That's the job of the messenger, and Jesus says it's John. I know a little something about preparing, friends, because my ovens never stop.

The answer is True! Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist." (Matthew 11:11). He opens with "Truly I tell you…" so you know He means it. Nobody born of women has risen greater than John, which is a high compliment.

The answer is the least in the kingdom of heaven. Jesus says, "Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he." (Matthew 11:11). He's just said that no one born of women has risen greater than John. Then the "yet" lands, and it's the least in the kingdom of heaven. That one made me stop and think.

The answer is Elijah. Jesus says, "And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come." (Matthew 11:14). He says it plainly. It comes with an "…if you are willing…" so He leaves it to the crowd to take it in.

The answer is children. Jesus says this generation is "…like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others…" (Matthew 11:16). It's a picture of kids who want the others to join in. The comparison is simple, and Jesus uses it on purpose to make a point.

The answer is that they say, "He has a demon." Jesus says, "For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon!’" (Matthew 11:18). That's a hard thing to say about anybody. I think it must have stung to have people say that about John.

The answer is False. Jesus says the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" (Matthew 11:19). John came one way and got one complaint, and Jesus came the other way and got a different complaint. Nobody was handing out gold stars.
